questions.prompt: A crate of mass $80\text{ kg}$ is held in the position shown. Taking $g = 9.81\text{ m/s}^2$, determine the magnitude of the moment produced by the weight $\mathbf{W}$ of the crate about edge $E$.
questions.solution: The weight of the crate is $W = mg = (80\text{ kg})(9.81\text{ m/s}^2) = 784.8\text{ N}$ acting vertically downward through the center of the crate ($0.6\text{ m}$ from the right face $BD$). Since edge $E$ lies $0.85\text{ m}$ to the left of the right face $BD$, the horizontal moment arm from $E$ to the line of action of $\mathbf{W}$ is $d = 0.85\text{ m} - 0.60\text{ m} = 0.25\text{ m}$. Therefore, $M_E = Wd = (784.8\text{ N})(0.25\text{ m}) = 196.2\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ (clockwise).

questions.prompt: Connecting rod $AB$ exerts a $500\text{-lb}$ force on crank $BC$ directed down and to the left along the centerline of $AB$. Determine the magnitude of the moment of this force about point $C$ (in $\text{kip}\cdot\text{in.}$).
questions.solution: From the geometry, $\overrightarrow{BA} = -(1.68\text{ in.})\mathbf{i} + (5.76\text{ in.})\mathbf{j}$, which has length $AB = \sqrt{1.68^2 + 5.76^2} = 6.00\text{ in.}$ Directed down and left along $AB$, the force is $\mathbf{F} = 500\left(-\frac{1.68}{6.00}\mathbf{i} - \frac{5.76}{6.00}\mathbf{j}\right) = -(140\text{ lb})\mathbf{i} - (480\text{ lb})\mathbf{j}$. With $\mathbf{r}_{B/C} = -(1.68\text{ in.})\mathbf{i} + (2.24\text{ in.})\mathbf{j}$, the moment about $C$ is $M_C = (-1.68)(-480) - (2.24)(-140) = 806.4 + 313.6 = 1120\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.} = 1.120\text{ kip}\cdot\text{in.}$ counterclockwise.

questions.prompt: A force with a moment of $960\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ about base point $D$ is required to straighten fence post $CD$. If distance $d = 2.80\text{ m}$, determine the required tension in cable $CB$ of winch puller $AB$.
questions.solution: Taking $D$ as the origin, point $C$ is at $(0.20\text{ m}, 0.875\text{ m})$ and anchor $E$ is at $(-2.80\text{ m}, 0)$. The vector along the cable from $C$ to $E$ is $\overrightarrow{CE} = -(3.00\text{ m})\mathbf{i} - (0.875\text{ m})\mathbf{j}$, with length $CE = \sqrt{3.00^2 + 0.875^2} = 3.125\text{ m}$. Moving the cable force along its line of action to $E$ eliminates the horizontal component's moment about $D$, leaving $M_D = (2.80\text{ m})\,T\left(\frac{0.875}{3.125}\right) = 0.784\,T$. Setting $0.784\,T = 960\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ gives $T = 1224\text{ N}$.

questions.prompt: A $200\text{-N}$ force is applied as shown at point $C$ of bracket $ABC$ (in a plane parallel to the $yz$ plane, $30^\circ$ from the vertical toward $+z$). Determine the moment vector $\mathbf{M}_A$ of the force about point $A$.
questions.solution: From the figure, the position vector from $A$ to $C$ is $\mathbf{r}_{C/A} = (0.060\text{ m})\mathbf{i} + (0.075\text{ m})\mathbf{j}$, and the $200\text{-N}$ force has components $\mathbf{F} = -(200\cos 30^\circ)\mathbf{j} + (200\sin 30^\circ)\mathbf{k} = -(173.21\text{ N})\mathbf{j} + (100\text{ N})\mathbf{k}$. Evaluating $\mathbf{M}_A = \mathbf{r}_{C/A} \times \mathbf{F}$ gives $(0.075\times 100)\mathbf{i} - (0.060\times 100)\mathbf{j} + (0.060\times(-173.21))\mathbf{k} = (7.50\text{ N}\cdot\text{m})\mathbf{i} - (6.00\text{ N}\cdot\text{m})\mathbf{j} - (10.39\text{ N}\cdot\text{m})\mathbf{k}$.

questions.prompt: Consider the volleyball net shown, with $A(0, 8, 0)\text{ ft}$, $C(0, 0, 6)\text{ ft}$, and $D(4, 0, 1)\text{ ft}$. Determine the angle (in degrees) formed by guy wires $AC$ and $AD$.
questions.solution: Write the vectors from $A$: $\overrightarrow{AC} = -(8\text{ ft})\mathbf{j} + (6\text{ ft})\mathbf{k}$ ($AC = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = 10\text{ ft}$) and $\overrightarrow{AD} = (4\text{ ft})\mathbf{i} - (8\text{ ft})\mathbf{j} + (1\text{ ft})\mathbf{k}$ ($AD = \sqrt{4^2 + (-8)^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{81} = 9\text{ ft}$). Their dot product is $\overrightarrow{AC} \cdot \overrightarrow{AD} = 0 + 64 + 6 = 70$. Hence $\cos\theta = \frac{70}{(10)(9)} = 0.7778$, giving $\theta = 38.9^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Given the three vectors $\mathbf{P} = 4\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} + 3\mathbf{k}$, $\mathbf{Q} = 2\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} - 5\mathbf{k}$, and $\mathbf{S} = S_x\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}$, determine the value of $S_x$ for which the three vectors are coplanar.
questions.solution: Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their mixed triple product vanishes: $\mathbf{S}\cdot(\mathbf{P}\times\mathbf{Q}) = \begin{vmatrix} S_x & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & -5 \end{vmatrix} = 0$. Expanding along the first row gives $S_x(10 - 12) - (-1)(-20 - 6) + 2(16 + 4) = -2S_x - 26 + 40 = 0 \implies 2S_x = 14 \implies S_x = 7$.

questions.prompt: A small boat hangs from the davit shown. The moment about the $z$ axis of the resultant force $\mathbf{R}_A$ exerted on the davit at $A$ must not exceed $279\text{ lb}\cdot\text{ft}$ in absolute value. Determine the largest allowable tension in line $ABAD$ when $x = 6\text{ ft}$.
questions.solution: Point $A$ has coordinates $(0, 7.75, 3)\text{ ft}$ and $D$ is at $(6, 0, 0)\text{ ft}$, so $\overrightarrow{AD} = 6\mathbf{i} - 7.75\mathbf{j} - 3\mathbf{k}$ with length $AD = \sqrt{6^2 + (-7.75)^2 + (-3)^2} = 10.25\text{ ft}$. At $A$, the vertical segment $AB$ exerts $-T\mathbf{j}$ (zero $x$-component) and segment $AD$ exerts $T(\overrightarrow{AD}/AD)$, so $(R_A)_x = T(6/10.25)$ and $(R_A)_y = -T - T(7.75/10.25)$. Since $x_A = 0$, the moment about the $z$ axis is $M_z = x_A(R_A)_y - y_A(R_A)_x = -7.75\,T(6/10.25) = -4.5366\,T$. Setting $|M_z| = 279\text{ lb}\cdot\text{ft}$ yields $T = 279 / 4.5366 = 61.5\text{ lb}$.

questions.prompt: A single force $\mathbf{P}$ acts at $C$ in a direction perpendicular to handle $BC$ of the crank shown ($OA = 150\text{ mm}$ along $+x$, $AB = 200\text{ mm}$ in a plane parallel to $yz$ at angle $\theta$ above $+z$, and $BC = 100\text{ mm}$ parallel to $+x$). Determine the moment $M_x$ of $\mathbf{P}$ about the $x$ axis when $\theta = 65^\circ$, knowing that $M_y = -15\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ and $M_z = -36\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$.
questions.solution: Because $\mathbf{P}$ is perpendicular to handle $BC$ (parallel to $+x$), $P_x = 0$. The coordinates of $C$ at $\theta = 65^\circ$ are $x_C = 0.150 + 0.100 = 0.250\text{ m}$, $y_C = 0.200\sin 65^\circ = 0.18126\text{ m}$, and $z_C = 0.200\cos 65^\circ = 0.08452\text{ m}$. From $M_y = z_C P_x - x_C P_z = -0.250 P_z = -15$, we get $P_z = 60\text{ N}$; from $M_z = x_C P_y - y_C P_x = 0.250 P_y = -36$, we get $P_y = -144\text{ N}$. Thus $M_x = y_C P_z - z_C P_y = (0.18126)(60) - (0.08452)(-144) = 23.05 \approx 23.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$.

questions.prompt: Frame $ACD$ is hinged at $A(0, 0, 0.75)\text{ m}$ and $D(1.0, 0, 0)\text{ m}$ and supported by a cable through ring $B(0.5, 0, 0.75)\text{ m}$ attached to hooks $G$ and $H(0.875, 0.75, 0)\text{ m}$. If the cable tension is $450\text{ N}$, determine the moment $M_{AD}$ (signed, in $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$) about diagonal $AD$ of the force exerted on the frame by portion $BH$ of the cable.
questions.solution: First compute the cable force along $\overrightarrow{BH} = 0.375\mathbf{i} + 0.75\mathbf{j} - 0.75\mathbf{k}$ ($BH = 1.125\text{ m}$): $\mathbf{F} = \frac{450}{1.125}(0.375\mathbf{i} + 0.75\mathbf{j} - 0.75\mathbf{k}) = 150\mathbf{i} + 300\mathbf{j} - 300\mathbf{k}\text{ N}$. The unit vector along $\overrightarrow{AD} = 1.0\mathbf{i} - 0.75\mathbf{k}$ ($AD = 1.25\text{ m}$) is $\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{AD} = 0.8\mathbf{i} - 0.6\mathbf{k}$, and $\mathbf{r}_{B/A} = 0.5\mathbf{i}\text{ m}$. Evaluating the mixed triple product $\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{AD}\cdot(\mathbf{r}_{B/A}\times\mathbf{F}) = \begin{vmatrix} 0.8 & 0 & -0.6 \\ 0.5 & 0 & 0 \\ 150 & 300 & -300 \end{vmatrix} = -0.6(150) = -90.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$.

questions.prompt: A piece of plywood is secured to a workbench by two nails. Knowing that the drill exerts a $12\text{-N}\cdot\text{m}$ couple on the plywood, determine the magnitude of the resulting forces applied to the nails if they are located at $B$ and $C$ ($240\text{ mm}$ apart).
questions.solution: To balance the $12\text{-N}\cdot\text{m}$ drill couple, the two nails at $B$ and $C$ must develop a couple of equal magnitude $M = Fd = 12\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$. With $d = BC = 0.240\text{ m}$, the force on each nail is $F = \frac{12\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}}{0.240\text{ m}} = 50.0\text{ N}$.

questions.prompt: A $30\text{-lb}$ vertical downward force $\mathbf{P}$ is applied at $A$ to the bracket shown, which is held by screws at $B$ and $C$. Which option gives BOTH (a) the equivalent force-couple system at $B$ and (b) the magnitude of the two horizontal forces at $B$ and $C$ equivalent to that couple?

options.label: A
options.text: $\mathbf{F} = 30.0\text{ lb}\downarrow,\; M_B = 150.0\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.}$ ccw; $50.0\text{ lb}$ horizontal forces

options.label: B
options.text: $\mathbf{F} = 30.0\text{ lb}\downarrow,\; M_B = 150.0\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.}$ cw; $50.0\text{ lb}$ horizontal forces

options.label: C
options.text: $\mathbf{F} = 30.0\text{ lb}\downarrow,\; M_B = 60.0\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.}$ ccw; $20.0\text{ lb}$ horizontal forces

options.label: D
options.text: $\mathbf{F} = 30.0\text{ lb}\downarrow,\; M_B = 150.0\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.}$ ccw; $75.0\text{ lb}$ horizontal forces

questions.solution: Moving the $30\text{-lb}$ downward force from $A$ to $B$ ($5\text{ in.}$ horizontally to the right) requires adding a couple equal to the moment of $\mathbf{P}$ about $B$: $M_B = (30\text{ lb})(5\text{ in.}) = 150.0\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.}$ counterclockwise. Replacing this $150.0\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.}$ ccw couple with two horizontal forces separated vertically by $d = BC = 3\text{ in.}$ requires $F = \frac{150.0}{3} = 50.0\text{ lb}$ (pointing right at $B$ and left at $C$).

questions.prompt: The shearing forces on a steel channel cross section consist of a $900\text{-N}$ vertical downward force along $BD$ and two $250\text{-N}$ horizontal forces ($180\text{ mm}$ apart, top right, bottom left). Replace this system with a single force $\mathbf{F}$ applied at the shear center $C$, and determine the distance $x$ from $C$ to line $BD$.
questions.solution: The two $250\text{-N}$ horizontal forces form a clockwise couple of magnitude $M = (250\text{ N})(180\text{ mm}) = 45{,}000\text{ N}\cdot\text{mm} = 45.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$. Moving the $900\text{-N}$ downward force to the right by distance $x$ to point $C$ produces a clockwise moment $(900\text{ N})x$ about $BD$. Equating moments: $900x = 45{,}000 \implies x = 50.0\text{ mm}$.

questions.prompt: An antenna is guyed by three cables as shown, with $A(0, 128, 0)\text{ ft}$ and $B(-64, 0, 16)\text{ ft}$. Knowing that the tension in cable $AB$ is $288\text{ lb}$, replace the force exerted at $A$ by cable $AB$ with an equivalent force-couple system at the base center $O$.
questions.solution: From $A(0,128,0)$ to $B(-64,0,16)$, $\overrightarrow{AB} = -64\mathbf{i} - 128\mathbf{j} + 16\mathbf{k}\text{ ft}$ with length $AB = \sqrt{64^2+128^2+16^2} = 144\text{ ft}$. Thus $\mathbf{F} = \frac{288}{144}(-64\mathbf{i} - 128\mathbf{j} + 16\mathbf{k}) = -(128.0\text{ lb})\mathbf{i} - (256\text{ lb})\mathbf{j} + (32.0\text{ lb})\mathbf{k}$. Moving $\mathbf{F}$ to $O$ requires $\mathbf{M}_O = \mathbf{r}_{A/O}\times\mathbf{F} = (128\mathbf{j})\times(-128\mathbf{i}-256\mathbf{j}+32\mathbf{k}) = 4096\mathbf{i} + 16384\mathbf{k}\text{ lb}\cdot\text{ft} = (4.10\text{ kip}\cdot\text{ft})\mathbf{i} + (16.38\text{ kip}\cdot\text{ft})\mathbf{k}$.

questions.prompt: Three stage lights are mounted on a pipe as shown. Lights $A$ and $B$ each weigh $4.1\text{ lb}$, while light $C$ weighs $3.5\text{ lb}$. If $d = 25\text{ in.}$, determine the distance from end $D$ to the line of action of the resultant weight.
questions.solution: The total downward resultant weight is $R = 4.1 + 4.1 + 3.5 = 11.7\text{ lb}$. The positions from $D$ are $x_A = 10\text{ in.}$, $x_B = 10 + 34 = 44\text{ in.}$, and $x_C = 44 + 25 = 69\text{ in.}$ Equating the moment of $R$ about $D$ to the sum of moments gives $11.7\,x = (4.1)(10) + (4.1)(44) + (3.5)(69) = 41 + 180.4 + 241.5 = 462.9\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.}$, so $x = 462.9 / 11.7 = 39.6\text{ in.}$

questions.prompt: The forces and couples shown ($10\text{ lb}\downarrow$ and $6\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.}$ clockwise looking down $y$ at $A$ with $z = 20\text{ in.}$; $11\text{ lb}\downarrow$ and $6\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.}$ clockwise looking down $y$ at $B$ with $z = -15\text{ in.}$) are applied to two screws. Reduce the system to an equivalent wrench and determine the pitch $p$ of the wrench.
questions.solution: Summing forces gives $\mathbf{R} = -(10 + 11)\mathbf{j} = -(21.0\text{ lb})\mathbf{j}$. Summing moments about $O$ gives $\mathbf{M}_O^R = (20\mathbf{k})\times(-10\mathbf{j}) + (-15\mathbf{k})\times(-11\mathbf{j}) - 6\mathbf{j} - 6\mathbf{j} = (200 - 165)\mathbf{i} - 12\mathbf{j} = (35\mathbf{i} - 12\mathbf{j})\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in.}$ Using Eq. (3.62), the pitch is $p = \frac{\mathbf{R}\cdot\mathbf{M}_O^R}{R^2} = \frac{(-21)(-12)}{(-21)^2} = \frac{12}{21} = 0.571\text{ in.}$

questions.prompt: The tailgate of a car is supported by hydraulic lift $BC$. If the lift exerts a $125\text{-lb}$ force directed along its centerline from $C$ toward $B$ on the ball-and-socket at $B$, determine the magnitude of the moment of this force about hinge $A$ (in $\text{lb}\cdot\text{ft}$).
questions.solution: Taking hinge $A$ as the origin, $C$ lies at $(3.3, -12.0)\text{ in.}$ and $B$ lies at $(15.3, -14.33)\text{ in.}$, so $\overrightarrow{CB} = 12.0\mathbf{i} - 2.33\mathbf{j}\text{ in.}$ with length $CB = \sqrt{12.0^2 + (-2.33)^2} = 12.224\text{ in.}$ Thus $\mathbf{F} = \frac{125}{12.224}(12.0\mathbf{i} - 2.33\mathbf{j})\text{ lb}$. Using point $C$ on the line of action of $\mathbf{F}$ with $\mathbf{r}_{C/A} = \frac{3.3\mathbf{i} - 12.0\mathbf{j}}{12}\text{ ft}$, the moment about $A$ is $M_A = \frac{125}{(12)(12.224)}[(3.3)(-2.33) - (-12.0)(12.0)] = 0.8521(136.31) = 116.2\text{ lb}\cdot\text{ft}$ counterclockwise.
